PullRequest.Title: chat: match pins across a model's copies in editor and Agents windows
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #346046, which shared pin storage between the Editor and Agents windows but merged before this fix. Fixes the remaining case of #345882.

## Problem

The same model has a different identifier in each window, so even with shared storage, pins didn't carry over in either direction:

- The Editor window's Copilot picker stores a pin as `copilot/<id>`, but the Agents window offers the same model as `agent-host-copilotcli:<id>`.
- Codex and Claude qualify ids with the provider they reach a model through, such as `codex:@provider=vscode-proxy:gpt-5.6-sol` and `claude:@provider=copilot:claude-opus-4.6`.
- Agent host copies of models users bring from extensions also get new identifiers.

## Change

`LanguageModelsService` now stores and matches pins by an identity:

- Built-in models (`BUILT_IN_GROUP_IDS`: the extension, the CLI harness, and agent host copies in the `copilot` group) share the extension's identifier, `copilot/<id>`. Provider-qualified ids are decoded first, so Codex's and Claude's Copilot copies match too. Their ChatGPT and Anthropic copies group under `chatgpt` and `anthropic`, so they stay separate.
- Agent host copies of extension-provided models share the original identifier from `byokModelIdentifier`, which the picker already uses to match hidden models.
- Auto, which routes differently per harness, and all other models keep their own identifiers.

`getPinnedModelIds()` returns every available copy of a pinned model, `isModelPinned()` matches any copy, pinning stores the identity, and unpinning removes every entry for it. Existing Editor pins already use these identities, so nothing is migrated.

The `@provider=<provider>:<modelId>` format was implemented separately for Codex (`codexModelSelection.ts`) and Claude (`claudeModelSelection.ts`). It now lives in `platform/agentHost/common/providerQualifiedModelId.ts`, which both parsers and the pin identity use. The parsers' behavior is unchanged.

## Notes for reviewers

- Hidden models still match by plain identifier, because whether hiding a model in one window should hide its copy in the other needs a product decision. Recently used models are being removed in #346053.

## How to test

1. In an Editor window on the default profile, pin a Copilot model and a model from an extension provider in the chat model picker.
2. Open the Agents window and its model picker, including a Codex or Claude session: the Copilot copies of those models are pinned, and the ChatGPT or Anthropic copies are not.
3. Unpin one in the Agents window: it's unpinned in the Editor window too.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <file>` for `languageModels.test.ts`, `sessionModelSelection.test.ts`, `agentHostLanguageModelProvider.test.ts`, `chatModelsViewModel.test.ts`, `modelPickerTelemetry.test.ts`, `claudeModelSelection.test.ts`, `claudeAgent.test.ts`, `codexModelSelection.test.ts`, `codexCreateChat.test.ts`, `codexModelRefresh.test.ts` and `codexPrewarmEviction.test.ts`: 967 passing
- The new regression test fails without pin identities, and fails without decoding provider-qualified ids.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed
- End to end in Code OSS with both windows: not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the chat model picker or cycle to the next pinned model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After model discovery, getPinnedModelIds synchronously walks the in-memory model cache, groups identifiers by pin identity, and returns matching available copies before the picker can render or the cycle command can choose a model. Model discovery itself is unchanged and is not initiated by the new identity helper.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total resolved models M, stored pin identities P, and the number of available vendor/harness copies per identity C. The pass is O(M + P*C); although the implementation copies each per-identity array while grouping, effective C is bounded by the small set of extension/CLI/Codex/Claude copies rather than M, so realistic cost remains near-linear.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entire pin-query computation is synchronous with no queue or parallel work. Existing vendor model resolution is independently sequenced/coalesced per vendor and is not changed by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model cache is the authoritative warm cache. On a cold/unresolved cache, no available copies are returned, as before unavailable stored pins were filtered out; subsequent model resolution populates the cache. The diff adds no retained identity cache, miss retry, or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds an in-memory model-cache scan and small allocations on each query; callers and cache ownership are directly traced. It does not add an external boundary or hot per-frame invocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installations can have varying numbers of extension/BYOK models, but picker opening and pinned cycling are user-triggered, and duplicate copies per identity remain small. No evidence supports user-visible latency at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The query is more expensive than the prior O(P) filter, but remains bounded, user-triggered, in-memory work at realistic model counts and copy multiplicity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or interact with rows in the Manage Language Models table
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible model rows synchronously call isModelPinned while rendering pin actions; context-menu creation may call it for each selected row. The new implementation resolves the candidate identity and scans stored pins, all in memory, before actions are shown.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible/selected model rows R and stored pins P. Both before and after the diff the membership check scales O(R*P); the diff adds cache lookups and provider-ID decoding for built-in entries but does not increase asymptotic cardinality. Table virtualization bounds normal row rendering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work only; no async fan-out is started by isModelPinned.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Metadata is read from the existing model cache. Unknown/stale stored identifiers fall back to their literal identifier without creating or retaining cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the row renderer and context-menu call sites that checks occur per rendered/selected row and remain in-memory.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: P is user-controlled and not explicitly capped, but it was already scanned by Array.includes for each row and ordinarily tracks a small curated list. The added constant-factor identity work is insufficient for a concrete regression finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no new scaling class, boundary, retained state, or realistic dropped-frame mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pin or unpin a model, including cross-window copies and multi-selection in Manage Models
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A pin checks identity membership, stores one normalized identity, writes preferences, logs telemetry, and emits the existing change event. Unpin filters equivalent stored identities, then performs the same existing write/log/event sequence. In the Manage Models view, that event still invokes the pre-existing refresh path that resolves vendors before rebuilding rows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the pinned-model identifier array through IStorageService.store
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per successful pin or unpin action; equivalent-copy operations can now be coalesced into no-ops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful pin/unpin already performed one storage write; the diff changes stored identifiers but does not add writes and can reduce them for duplicate copies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing storage call occurs before the action emits its change event and completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One telemetry event per successful pin/unpin, unchanged; equivalent-copy no-ops can reduce events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same telemetry call occurred once after every successful mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry API invocation remains on the action path, while transport batching/network behavior is owned downstream and unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve language-model information from registered providers via provideLanguageModelChatInfo during the Manage Models refresh triggered by the existing pin-change listener
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one joined/queued resolution per vendor per refresh request under the existing per-vendor sequencer; successful mutations emit the same event as before, while equivalent duplicates can emit fewer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every successful pin/unpin already fired onDidChangePinnedModels, whose listener called the same refresh and provider-resolution path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Manage Models waits for provider resolution before rebuilding all vendor rows; this pre-existing refresh is not added or moved by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Stored pins P per action; multi-selection count S. Identity matching adds O(P) in-memory work per action. Equivalent copies are now coalesced, so later pin/unpin calls for the same identity can return without duplicate writes, telemetry, events, or refreshes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pin identity work is synchronous. Existing model refresh uses per-vendor SequencerByKey queues and joins queued resolutions; the diff does not alter this scheduling. Multi-selection still invokes actions serially in its loop, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pin identity is derived from the current authoritative model cache; stored identities persist through the existing storage service. No new cache or retained map survives a call. Cross-window storage listeners reload the same bounded persisted array.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the storage, telemetry, event, and provider-refresh call flow and in the diff's unchanged or reduced boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider resolution duration varies by installed provider, but the diff neither introduces that boundary nor increases successful mutation events for a given action sequence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Added O(P) identity work is small relative to existing explicit-action boundaries, and coalescing equivalent copies can reduce duplicate boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Encode, restore, switch, or dispatch a Codex/Claude provider-qualified model selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extracted helper performs the same prefix check, separator search, URL decoding, and fallback behavior synchronously before existing model lookup, transport selection, subprocess switching, or request dispatch proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the parsed Claude provider/model to select or rebuild the existing Claude subprocess transport on a later send
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the same transport decision/rebuild per actual cross-transport model switch as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The module-local parser returned the same provider/model/explicit-provider result and drove the same rebuild decision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cross-transport switch may require the existing subprocess rebuild on the next send; helper extraction does not add, duplicate, or move this boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch an existing Codex or Claude model request through the selected provider/transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing request per user send; parser extraction does not alter request count or fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent module-local encode/decode logic selected the provider before the same request dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider parsing precedes dispatch but adds no extra network operation and preserves the same decoding algorithm.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One model identifier per selection operation, plus existing catalog scans where callers already parse each candidate. Identifier length and catalog size are unchanged by the extraction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parsing is synchronous and constant per identifier. Existing model-refresh sequencing, Claude subprocess lifecycle, and request concurrency are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved or added; encoding/decoding remains stateless. Warm and cold behavior are identical.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the deleted and added parser bodies are mechanically equivalent and all call sites continue through the wrapper functions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Downstream subprocess and network latencies vary, but their occurrence, scheduling, and cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance change; this is a shared-helper refactor with unchanged per-identifier CPU and unchanged external boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and complete diff pages under the performance focus. Traced pin queries through picker commands and virtualized Manage Models rendering, pin mutations through storage/telemetry/provider refresh, and shared provider-ID parsing through Codex/Claude dispatch and subprocess paths. The PR adds bounded in-memory identity matching and allocations but no realistic hot-path or boundary amplification; equivalent-copy coalescing can reduce duplicate mutation work. No performance findings or regression-fix learning record are warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
